patterns.label: Cache-aside
patterns.detail: The application reads the source on a miss and owns population and invalidation.
patterns.authority: The source database is authoritative; the cache is a disposable read copy.
patterns.path: Read: app -> cache -> source on miss -> cache. Write: app -> source -> delete or version cache key.

patterns.label: Read-through
patterns.detail: The cache provider loads a miss from a configured source adapter.
patterns.authority: The source database remains authoritative; the cache owns miss loading policy.
patterns.path: Read: app -> cache -> source adapter on miss. Write: application still commits source and refreshes or invalidates cache.

patterns.label: Write-through
patterns.detail: A write updates the cache and durable source in one synchronous flow.
patterns.authority: The durable source is authoritative after the write completes; the cache mirrors the acknowledged value.
patterns.path: Read: app -> cache. Write: app -> cache write path -> durable source -> acknowledgement.

patterns.label: Write-behind
patterns.detail: A cache accepts a write and flushes it to the source asynchronously.
patterns.authority: Before flush, the cache holds accepted but not yet durable state; after flush, the source is durable authority.
patterns.path: Read: app -> cache. Write: app -> cache -> asynchronous flush queue -> source.

patterns.label: Event invalidation
patterns.detail: A committed source write emits an event that removes or versions derived cache entries.
patterns.authority: The source database is authoritative; an outbox event distributes cache coherence work.
patterns.path: Write: app -> source transaction + outbox -> event consumer -> invalidate or version cache entries.

scenarios.label: Stale write or lost invalidation
scenarios.detail: A source record changes while a previous cache value can still be served.

scenarios.label: Source outage
scenarios.detail: The database is unavailable while reads or writes continue to arrive.

scenarios.label: Synchronized expiry
scenarios.detail: Many popular keys expire at the same time and miss together.

scenarios.label: Hot key
scenarios.detail: One key receives a disproportionate share of traffic.

scenarios.label: Regional partition
scenarios.detail: Regions cannot exchange invalidations or reach a shared source reliably.

stale-write.staleRisk: High when deletion is lost or ordered before the source commit.
stale-write.duplicateRisk: Low for reads; retries of the application write still need idempotency.
stale-write.blastRadius: Usually one key or tag, but a bad namespace can invalidate a whole feature.
stale-write.recovery: Commit source first, then delete or version the key. Re-read from source and repair the affected cache namespace.

source-outage.staleRisk: Controlled only if stale-if-error is explicitly allowed and bounded.
source-outage.duplicateRisk: Low for reads; reject or queue writes rather than pretending they committed.
source-outage.blastRadius: Every cold key becomes an unavailable read; hot cached keys may remain available.
source-outage.recovery: Serve bounded stale data only for safe reads, use circuit breaking, and warm priority keys after source recovery.

synchronized-expiry.staleRisk: Low, but source pressure can turn misses into user-visible failures.
synchronized-expiry.duplicateRisk: Many identical source reads can run concurrently without request coalescing.
synchronized-expiry.blastRadius: All keys sharing a TTL boundary can overload the source pool.
synchronized-expiry.recovery: Add TTL jitter, singleflight or leases, and negative caching for known absent keys.

hot-key.staleRisk: Depends on invalidation delivery; a hot stale value is highly visible.
hot-key.duplicateRisk: Low, unless each miss triggers an independent refresh.
hot-key.blastRadius: One key can saturate a cache shard or reconnecting clients.
hot-key.recovery: Coalesce refreshes, replicate or shard the hot value deliberately, and rate-limit abusive clients.

regional-partition.staleRisk: Regions can serve divergent copies until TTL or reconciliation closes the gap.
regional-partition.duplicateRisk: Write retries across regions can repeat work without an idempotency key.
regional-partition.blastRadius: One region can drift; a global cache key makes the failure wider.
regional-partition.recovery: Choose a write region, fence conflicting writers, expire or version on reconnection, and reconcile durable records.

stale-write.staleRisk: Medium: read loading is centralized, but writes still need a source-first invalidation rule.
stale-write.duplicateRisk: Low for reads; adapter retries must not repeat mutations.
stale-write.blastRadius: A faulty adapter policy can affect every key using that cache cluster.
stale-write.recovery: Make the source commit and cache version explicit; invalidate affected keys and verify adapter observability.

source-outage.staleRisk: Bounded only by explicit stale serving; misses fail at the adapter boundary.
source-outage.duplicateRisk: Low for reads; writes must report uncertainty rather than rely on a read adapter.
source-outage.blastRadius: Cold reads across the adapter fail together when its source dependency is down.
source-outage.recovery: Use a short circuit breaker and a documented stale-if-error window for safe resources.

synchronized-expiry.staleRisk: Low, but the adapter can create a coordinated miss storm.
synchronized-expiry.duplicateRisk: Duplicate loads are possible unless the cache coalesces them.
synchronized-expiry.blastRadius: Cluster-wide TTL alignment can overload the source adapter and database.
synchronized-expiry.recovery: Use per-key jitter and provider-supported request collapsing or refresh-ahead for proven hot keys.

hot-key.staleRisk: Medium if refresh is delayed; a hot key magnifies one cache policy error.
hot-key.duplicateRisk: Concurrent loads may duplicate source reads.
hot-key.blastRadius: A single cache node or source connection pool can become the bottleneck.
hot-key.recovery: Pin or replicate carefully, collapse loads, and verify the adapter has per-key metrics.

regional-partition.staleRisk: Regional adapters may read different source replicas or retain isolated values.
regional-partition.duplicateRisk: Cross-region write retries remain an application concern.
regional-partition.blastRadius: The partition is scoped to the affected region unless cache routing is global.
regional-partition.recovery: Use regional authority and reconciliation rules; do not assume read-through creates cross-region coherence.

stale-write.staleRisk: Low only when the cache and durable source acknowledge the same version; split failures remain possible.
stale-write.duplicateRisk: A retry after an uncertain acknowledgement can repeat a write without an idempotency key.
stale-write.blastRadius: A broken synchronous write path blocks all writes using it.
stale-write.recovery: Use version checks and idempotency keys, then reconcile any cache/source disagreement before reopening writes.

source-outage.staleRisk: Reads may remain fresh enough, but synchronous writes should fail or queue explicitly.
source-outage.duplicateRisk: Retrying a timed-out write can duplicate an effect.
source-outage.blastRadius: Write availability is coupled to source availability.
source-outage.recovery: Reject or durably queue writes with a visible status; do not acknowledge a durable write that the source did not confirm.

synchronized-expiry.staleRisk: Low for recently written keys; cold-key read misses still fan into the source.
synchronized-expiry.duplicateRisk: Low for writes, possible for uncoalesced read fills.
synchronized-expiry.blastRadius: Read storms still pressure the source even though writes are synchronized.
synchronized-expiry.recovery: Jitter expiration, coalesce fills, and separate write capacity from read-miss capacity.

hot-key.staleRisk: Low when writes complete, but one hot mutable key serializes synchronous write latency.
hot-key.duplicateRisk: Client retries need idempotency around the write request.
hot-key.blastRadius: The hot key can consume cache and source write capacity.
hot-key.recovery: Serialize with a version or conditional write, publish read replicas carefully, and measure write contention.

regional-partition.staleRisk: Each region can acknowledge different versions if multi-writer replication is not fenced.
regional-partition.duplicateRisk: High for client retries that cross regions without a global key.
regional-partition.blastRadius: A synchronous cross-region dependency can make the partition global.
regional-partition.recovery: Prefer one write authority per key, fence stale leaders, and reconcile versions before re-enabling multi-region writes.

stale-write.staleRisk: High: readers can observe cache state that is not yet durable, and flush order matters.
stale-write.duplicateRisk: Flush retries can duplicate non-idempotent source mutations.
stale-write.blastRadius: A flush bug can corrupt or lose every queued write in a cache partition.
stale-write.recovery: Persist an ordered durable write log, make source writes idempotent, and replay with version checks.

source-outage.staleRisk: The cache can keep accepting writes, but the gap between accepted and durable state grows.
source-outage.duplicateRisk: Flush retries can repeat writes after recovery.
source-outage.blastRadius: A prolonged outage fills cache or write-log capacity and risks data loss on failure.
source-outage.recovery: Apply a durable queue limit, expose flush lag, stop accepting writes before capacity is exhausted, and replay idempotently.

synchronized-expiry.staleRisk: Expiry can discard accepted-but-unflushed state if the design does not protect it.
synchronized-expiry.duplicateRisk: Recovery replays can repeat source writes.
synchronized-expiry.blastRadius: Shared expiry settings can destroy a broad set of pending writes.
synchronized-expiry.recovery: Do not use ordinary eviction for pending writes; persist and drain a write-ahead log before eviction.

hot-key.staleRisk: Rapid updates can coalesce or reorder, hiding intermediate states from the source.
hot-key.duplicateRisk: A failed flush batch may replay more than one mutation.
hot-key.blastRadius: One hot key can monopolize a flush worker and delay unrelated writes.
hot-key.recovery: Partition ordered flushes by key, cap coalescing to allowed semantics, and alert on per-key flush lag.

regional-partition.staleRisk: Independent regional buffers can accept conflicting values while disconnected.
regional-partition.duplicateRisk: Both regions can flush the same logical mutation after reconnection.
regional-partition.blastRadius: Conflict resolution becomes a data-model problem, not a cache setting.
regional-partition.recovery: Avoid multi-writer write-behind unless conflicts are designed; fence writers or use a single durable log authority.

stale-write.staleRisk: Medium and bounded by event lag; a missing event leaves stale entries until TTL or repair.
stale-write.duplicateRisk: Events are commonly at-least-once, so invalidation consumers must tolerate duplicate delivery.
stale-write.blastRadius: A bad event schema or broad tag can invalidate a feature-wide cache namespace.
stale-write.recovery: Use a transactional outbox, versioned event IDs, replayable consumers, and periodic cache/source reconciliation.

source-outage.staleRisk: Existing entries can serve within a documented stale window; no new source commits should emit invalidations.
source-outage.duplicateRisk: Event retries after recovery are normal and should be harmless.
source-outage.blastRadius: Consumers may lag while the source or broker is down, widening freshness delay.
source-outage.recovery: Monitor outbox and consumer lag, pause unsafe writers, then replay events and invalidate affected versions.

synchronized-expiry.staleRisk: Low if events invalidate early, but expiry can still create a read-miss storm.
synchronized-expiry.duplicateRisk: Repeated invalidation events should be no-ops.
synchronized-expiry.blastRadius: A shared expiry boundary still overloads the read path if event freshness is not enough.
synchronized-expiry.recovery: Add TTL jitter, coalesce fills, and use versioned keys so late events cannot delete newer data.

hot-key.staleRisk: Fast event lag makes one hot key visibly stale; event fan-out may itself become hot.
hot-key.duplicateRisk: Duplicate events are expected and must not trigger repeated destructive work.
hot-key.blastRadius: A hot entity can flood invalidation consumers and evict a large fan-out of derived keys.
hot-key.recovery: Debounce where semantics permit, version derived keys, and isolate hot-key event partitions and metrics.

regional-partition.staleRisk: Regions miss invalidations and serve diverging versions until replay completes.
regional-partition.duplicateRisk: Replay after reconnection delivers duplicate events by design.
regional-partition.blastRadius: The isolated region drifts; global consumers can spread delayed invalidations on recovery.
regional-partition.recovery: Keep per-region event cursors, use monotonically increasing versions, replay from the durable log, and invalidate only older versions.
